Documentation → FortiWeb: Policies & Protection → Stored Assets

Stored assets

What an ADOM holds, per device - configuration backups on the backup server, the configuration SoT history and firmware images, plus SATOM's own backup bundles in the Global ADOM.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereAny ADOM → Administrator → Stored Assets (URL /adom-assets/)

What is it?#

Stored Assets answers one question per ADOM: what does SATOM hold for these devices? It brings four kinds of stored artifacts onto one page:

  1. Device config backups that the appliances wrote and pushed to the backup server.
  2. The Configuration SoT: the configuration history SATOM records itself at every harvest.
  3. Firmware images held to be installed onto a device.
  4. SATOM's own backup bundles. These are console-wide, so they appear in the Global ADOM only.

These four are separate things, with separate retention, and none of them is a copy of another. The page is not FortiWeb-specific: it exists in every ADOM and is scoped to the ADOM you are in. Global means every family.

ℹ️Note

The page only shows holdings. Retention and the backup server itself are set once for the whole console in Settings → Configuration SoT and Settings → Backup Server. Creating and restoring SATOM bundles happens on System Backup & Restore.

What does it do?#

  • Tiles for the whole ADOM: Devices (with the number retired), Backups on server, Never pushed, Stale (older than 8 days), SoT versions (with the number off-box), Firmware images (with total MB), and in Global SATOM backups. The tiles never change with the filter.
  • One row per device (chassis). A FortiWeb in ADOM mode is one appliance row per ADOM but has one flash and one backup file. Its ADOM rows are folded into the device, and their counts are added.
  • Last push grading for card 1:
State Meaning
never pushed No file has ever arrived for this device
unknown (server unreachable or no backup server) The backup server could not be read, or none is configured, so SATOM cannot tell (grey)
<n> day(s) ago, up to 8 days Healthy (green)
9 to 31 days Stale (orange)
more than 31 days Critical (red)
date unreadable Files exist but their timestamp could not be read
  • Arrangement: devices are grouped by family, then by your own bookmark grouping order (for example Product › Line › Zone › Department). The button at the top right names the order and links to your profile, where you change it.
  • Folding: every card and group starts folded. Expand all and Collapse all sit at the top right. What you open is remembered in this browser, per ADOM. The filter card never folds.
  • Global only: 1b · Unclaimed folders on the backup server (folders no device answers to), and a warning listing devices that have configuration history but no identity record.

Requirements#

  • A backup server configured under Settings → Backup Server, for card 1. Without it the page warns No backup server is configured, so nothing below can say whether a device is pushing its backups.
  • Appliances configured to push their backups to that server (an appliance-side backup job). SATOM does not create these files.

Permissions#

users.manage is required for every action on this page (Administrator). The entry is in the Administrator group, which is hidden without it. A direct request returns 403 Forbidden. The download links use System Backup's download endpoint, which has the same requirement.

The page is reachable from every ADOM, including FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator.

How to use#

Find devices that stopped pushing backups#

  1. Open Administrator → Stored Assets in the ADOM you care about.
  2. Look at the Never pushed and Stale tiles.
  3. In the Filter card, set Backup state to Stale or Never pushed and click Filter.
  4. Open 1 · Device config backups and the family headings to see the devices.

Search for a device by any name it has had#

  1. Type into Name, former name, serial, host or model (for example a serial number) and click Filter.
  2. The device cards show showing N of M.

The filter is part of the URL (type=, state=, q=, retired=hide), so a filtered view can be bookmarked or shared. Click Clear to drop it.

List or delete one backup file#

  1. In 1 · Device config backups, click Files on the device row. The 10 most recent files of each folder are listed with Modified and Size. When a folder holds more, the table says Showing the N newest of M files in this folder.
  2. Click the download button to fetch a file.
  3. To delete one, click the trash button and type DELETE in the prompt Type DELETE to remove <file> from the backup server.

Inside an ADOM you can delete files only from the folders of that ADOM's devices. The Global ADOM reaches every device folder.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: deleting a backup file is now limited to the device folders of the ADOM you are in (switch to Global to reach any folder), and while the backup server cannot be read devices show unknown instead of never pushed.

Reconcile identities#

  1. Click Reconcile identity in the Filter card header.
  2. The flash reports Identity reconciled: <n> new record(s), <n> adopted from history. SoT: <n> version(s) filed under an ADOM, <n> device(s) still unidentified.

Run it when a device appears without history, or when the Global ADOM lists devices with configuration history but no identity record. It is safe to run twice.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Device type Global only. A family, or unassigned for devices whose family is unknown No FortiWeb
Backup state Pushing, Stale (stale and critical), Never pushed, Unknown. Narrows card 1 only No Stale
Name, former name, serial, host or model Free text, max. 120 characters No FWB-0001
Hide de-registered devices Hides devices whose every row is retired. Nothing is removed No ticked

An unrecognised filter value narrows nothing rather than emptying the page.

Example#

🧪Example — Weekly backup check

An admin opens Stored Assets in the FortiWeb ADOM. The tiles show Devices 12, Never pushed 1 and Stale 2. Filtering on Never pushed shows fweb-07. It has 140 SoT versions in card 2 but has never pushed a file, so its backup job on the appliance was never configured. The two stale devices last pushed 12 and 40 days ago. The 40-day one is red. The admin fixes the appliance jobs and checks again the next day.

Result#

  • Filtering, folding and viewing change nothing.
  • Reconcile identity creates or adopts identity records and stamps the ADOM onto older SoT versions. Audit entry: adom_assets.reconcile.
  • Deleting a file removes exactly that file from the backup server. The audit entry adom_assets.delete_backup names the device, the file and the result, and is written whether or not the delete succeeded.

Troubleshooting#

"The backup server is not reachable"#

Possible causes - Wrong host, credentials or path in Settings → Backup Server, or a network problem.

Solution 1. Fix the connection in Settings → Backup Server. 2. Reload the page.

Verification - The red banner is gone and card 1 shows file counts.

While the server cannot be read, every device in card 1 shows unknown with the reason server unreachable, as the banner says. A device is never graded never pushed only because the server could not be listed.

"Not confirmed — type DELETE to remove a backup from the server."#

Possible causes - The prompt was cancelled, or something other than DELETE was typed.

Solution 1. Click the trash button again and type DELETE exactly.

Verification - The flash reads <device>/<file> (<n> KB) deleted from <host>.

"/ is not on the server"#

Possible causes - The file was already removed, or the appliance rotated it out.

Solution 1. Reload the page to get the current listing.

Verification - The file no longer appears under Files.

A device shows "no history" in card 2 but pushes backups#

Possible causes - SATOM has not harvested the device's configuration yet, or its history is filed under another identity.

Solution 1. Click Reconcile identity. 2. In the Global ADOM, check the warning about devices with configuration history and no identity record.

Verification - Card 2 shows a version count for the device.

Only some files are listed under "Files"#

Possible causes - The page lists the 10 most recent files per folder and says Showing the N newest of M files in this folder. The Backups column counts all of them.

Solution 1. Use System Backup & Restore or the backup server directly for older files.

Verification - The Backups count matches the number of files on the server.

Advanced#

Advanced Identity, serials and folding
  • Device identity lives in its own table with no foreign key to the appliance, so it outlives a de-registered device. Retiring a device sets a timestamp; nothing is deleted.
  • The identity is the serial number, read from the same status call the firmware probe already makes. An empty serial means "never observed" and never overwrites a known one.
  • A device is shown retired only when every one of its rows is retired.
  • Card 2 is not narrowed by Backup state. It shows the badge backup state not applied here, because a device that never pushed a file can still have a long SoT history.
  • The page lists the backup server in one SFTP round trip for the whole fleet.
  • GET /adom-assets/files?device=<folder> returns the full listing of one folder as JSON. The page itself does not use it.
  • The delete action is limited to the ADOM shown: inside an ADOM it refuses a folder that does not belong to one of that ADOM's devices. In the Global ADOM it reaches every device folder. Only the last path component of the folder and file names is used, so it cannot reach outside the configured backup path.
